reason: Self-audit of the frozen ForeSeal review package found that the 2026-09-10 correction — which repointed the implementation pin to a publicly fetchable tag after ForeSeal established that all four prior pins were unfetchable — fixed the prose and left the canonical machine-readable manifest uncorrected. The manifest that the terms themselves named as the source of truth still asserted a retired bond wallet, an unfunded $0 bond, an unfetchable local commit, no custody model, a single-key slash path that the live code now refuses, and a bilateral agreement that ForeSeal never made. Found by StillOS, not by ForeSeal.

previous.disposition: HISTORICAL — not moved, not rewritten, not deleted. It has been referenced externally and stays fetchable at the SHA above for audit. docs/FORESEAL_BILATERAL_TERMS_V1.md is retained verbatim in the tree and carries only a prepended supersession banner.

new.why_null: A document cannot contain its own commit hash. V1 tried: its Parties table claimed the tag resolved to cd0c3f630f92… when the tag actually resolved to c68e06aa2d69…, inside the very commit that was fixing stale pins. Resolve the tag instead — `git rev-list -n1 foreseal-bilateral-v1.1`, or the GitHub tags API — and verify content against manifest/manifest.json's per-file sha256 checksums, which are self-verifying and independent of any commit hash.

corrected_fields.was: Read by buildSlashDirective() but never written by anything, so it was permanently null and every upheld dispute emitted the placeholder '<disputant_payout_0x>' instead of a real payout address.
corrected_fields.now: Carried from the request as an optional, validated disputant_wallet. A bad or absent value degrades to null and the obligation records that no wallet was supplied rather than inventing one.

corrected_fields.was: The slash directive was an in-memory object returned to the caller plus a founder alert inside a swallowed try/catch. Nothing was persisted. If the alert failed and the caller discarded the response, an adjudicated debt left no trace.
corrected_fields.now: implementation/bond/slash_obligations.cjs — append-only, hash-chained obligation ledger opened synchronously on UPHELD before the reputation write, before the alert, and before any signature is sought. Not wrapped in a try/catch: failure to record the debt fails the request.
corrected_fields.class: no durable record of an adjudicated debt

corrected_fields.was: fileDispute() returned slash_directive and the HTTP handler discarded it. On an upheld dispute the disputant received only upheld:true and a receipt — nothing about the payout owed to them.
corrected_fields.now: The handler accepts an optional disputant_wallet and returns a payout_obligation block carrying obligation_id, state, amount, disputant, owed_at, custody_type, bond wallet, the exact payout calldata, and an explicit committed_payout_sla: null. Deployed and verified live 2026-09-11.

corrected_fields.was: The public bond endpoint — the surface a counterparty actually calls — reported only balance-derived `active: true` with no custody type and no obligation state. The separated health facts added in D17 lived only inside healthCheck(), which is used by the cron monitor. A funded Safe sitting on an overdue adjudicated payout would have presented as fine to anyone checking /bond.

checked_and_not_defects: manifest/manifest.sha256 matched manifest.json exactly at tag v1 (163dcbcc48be37cfa37466eff990d9ebcb313e26a573b25a054ad6ef1fa14bde). The manifest was internally sealed; its CONTENTS were stale.
The private copy at still-os-consciousness/docs/x402-2887/manifest/manifest.json was byte-identical to the published one. The two manifest locations had not diverged.
The published implementation/bond/*.cjs at tag v1 were byte-identical to the live /home/marcus/core copies. The publication itself was faithful — what it was published ALONGSIDE was wrong.
2 of the 5 manifest file checksums (verdict_dispute.cjs, keyring.cjs) were still accurate against live code.
The implementation pin in the human terms had already been correctly repointed to the tag on 2026-09-10. The unfetchable local SHA survived only in the manifest and the Parties table.

The dispute guards ForeSeal would exercise — claim_sha256 hash binding, settles_against mutation guard, INDETERMINATE on unreachable source, deterministic dedup — were all present, correct, and unchanged.
